mission: Teach DreamCo coding bots to safely master open-source libraries, retain executable knowledge, and invent productive new combinations and products without blindly copying code or creating dependency chaos.
learning_principle: Do not memorize every repository. Build a continuously refreshed capability graph of libraries, APIs, patterns, benchmarks, examples, licenses, constraints, and reusable skills, then retrieve the right knowledge for each task.
library_learning_pipeline: discover relevant libraries from trusted public indexes, official docs, package registries, standards, and source repositories
record exact project, version/revision, license, maintainer, activity, language, runtime, dependencies, platform support, security status, and official documentation
sandbox the exact revision before execution
run dependency, malware, secret, provenance, and license checks
read README, API docs, examples, tests, changelog, architecture docs, package metadata, and representative source files
generate a library capability map: what it does, what it does not do, inputs, outputs, extension points, failure modes, performance characteristics, and competing libraries
generate executable micro-fixtures that prove the major capabilities instead of relying on documentation claims
generate task recipes and agent skill cards for recurring use
benchmark the library against alternatives using identical fixtures
store only lawful reusable knowledge, references, summaries, tests, interfaces, and license-compliant artifacts
mark stale knowledge when versions, security status, APIs, or maintainers change

invention_engine.goal: Turn mastered primitives into useful new tools, products, automations, APIs, apps, bots, workflows, developer experiences, and shared infrastructure.
methods: compose two or more proven capabilities into a workflow that removes a real user step
wrap a difficult library behind a safer and simpler Buddy interface
turn repeated manual setup into one-click or one-command automation
convert a command-line capability into phone, web, API, or agent-accessible form
combine local-first libraries to replace unnecessary paid/cloud dependencies
add observability, testing, recovery, permissions, and upgrade support to fragile open-source workflows
identify capability gaps shared across multiple libraries and build a reusable abstraction
combine domain libraries with Buddy specialist knowledge to create vertical products
turn examples/tests into interactive learning tools or simulations
turn file formats and converters into cross-app interoperability features
turn data/analysis libraries into business decision tools
turn media libraries into creator workflows
turn game/3D libraries into education, simulation, prototyping, or visualization tools
turn developer libraries into self-service user features when safe
generate adapters that let multiple equivalent libraries share one canonical Buddy interface
reduce cost, latency, memory, battery, storage, network use, or human steps versus existing solutions
invention_engine.anti_novelty_rule: Do not build something merely because libraries can be combined. A proposed invention must solve a defined problem or create a measurable improvement over an existing workflow.

curriculum_levels.gate: Bot can accurately explain the library's purpose, boundaries, license, dependencies, and major APIs from current sources.
Bot can run and verify official/minimal examples in a sandbox.
Bot can create deterministic and failure-path fixtures for the main capabilities.
Bot can integrate the library behind a canonical interface without breaking shared guardrails.
Bot can diagnose representative failures and recover cleanly.
Bot can measure and improve latency, resources, cost, reliability, or usability.
Bot can benchmark alternatives with identical fixtures and explain tradeoffs.
Bot can propose multiple useful new applications/combinations and rank them with the invention scorecard.
A selected invention passes clean-code, tests, security/privacy, license, migration, upgrade, rollback, and benchmark gates.
Reusable skills, fixtures, and improvements are promoted to shared fleet infrastructure and affected bots retest.

coverage_strategy.reason: The open-source ecosystem changes continuously and contains millions of packages, versions, forks, abandoned projects, malicious packages, and overlapping tools.
priority_order: libraries needed by active benchmark gaps
top libraries for each tech job family
high-adoption and high-quality libraries in major ecosystems
emerging libraries with verified user value

memory_and_learning.preferred: retrieval plus executable skills plus benchmark evidence
memory_and_learning.avoid: stuffing whole libraries into prompts or treating old summaries as current truth

guardrails: never import license-incompatible code into DreamCo merely because it is public
do not execute untrusted install scripts with broad host permissions
do not treat GitHub stars as proof of quality
do not treat generated code as correct until tested
do not create duplicate DreamCo systems when an existing canonical owner can be extended
do not promote a library into shared infrastructure until security, maintenance, compatibility, and benchmark checks pass
keep provenance for learned skills and adopted components
require easy upgrade/removal paths for third-party dependencies
success_metrics: percentage of active coding tasks solved using verified skill cards
time to understand a new repository/library
number of useful inventions reaching verified prototype or production status
